report:
**Conclusion:** Your claim is supported by good randomized-trial evidence, with an important caveat: the evidence is for *reducing new breast-cancer diagnoses*, chiefly estrogen-receptor–positive disease, in appropriately selected postmenopausal women—not for proving fewer breast-cancer deaths.

- In the double-blind, placebo-controlled MAP.3 trial, 4,560 postmenopausal women at moderately increased risk received exemestane 25 mg/day or placebo. At median 35-month follow-up, invasive breast-cancer incidence was 0.19% versus 0.55% per year: a 65% relative reduction (hazard ratio 0.35). Invasive plus DCIS incidence was also lower (HR 0.47). [https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/Nejmoa1103507](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/Nejmoa1103507)

- This is a strong design, but follow-up was relatively short and event numbers small; therefore, durability after treatment and effects on mortality remain less certain. The absolute benefit depends substantially on a woman’s baseline risk.

- ASCO’s risk-reduction guideline includes exemestane (along with anastrozole, tamoxifen, and raloxifene) as an option to discuss with postmenopausal women at increased risk, with individualized consideration of adverse effects and comorbidities. [https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.19.01472](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.19.01472)

- Trade-offs matter: aromatase inhibitors can cause vasomotor and musculoskeletal symptoms and may adversely affect bone health; USPSTF likewise recommends offering risk-reducing drugs only when breast-cancer risk is increased and medication-harm risk is low. [https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/breast-cancer-medications-for-risk-reduction](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/breast-cancer-medications-for-risk-reduction)

In the US, prevention is not an FDA-labeled exemestane indication; its label is for breast-cancer treatment. [https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=9354d1a1-8e8c-4c6a-b7ad-d4fe14b10a8b&type=display](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=9354d1a1-8e8c-4c6a-b7ad-d4fe14b10a8b&type=display)
